1.title: Transition, Operate, Deliver and Support
1.text: Welcome to Module seven: Transition, Operate, Deliver and Support. It covers the exam area The eye til Product and Service Lifecycle. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Know the purpose of transition, operate, deliver and support. Define release, continuous delivery, continuous deployment, incident, event, reliability, S R E (site reliability engineering), observability, service request, disaster, problem, error and known error. Distinguish problem, error and known error. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The eye til Product and Service Lifecycle (ten percent). Exam format: forty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; twenty-six correct answers (sixty-five percent) pass. Validated against: the official eye til Foundation (Version five) syllabus, version five point zero (February two thousand twenty-six).

1.title: Transition
1.text: Transition. Purpose: move a new or changed product or service safely into live use with as little disruption as possible. Release. A version of a product, service or component made available for use. Continuous delivery. Every change is kept ready to release; the release itself is a decision (often manual). Continuous deployment. Every change that passes the tests is released to live automatically. Exam tip: Delivery equals ready to release, a person presses go. Deployment equals released automatically. The extra word "deployment" means no human gate.

1.title: Operate
1.text: Operate. Purpose: run the product so it performs as agreed, and handle incidents and events as they happen. Event. Any change of state that has significance for managing a product or service. Incident. An unplanned interruption or reduction in quality of a service. Reliability. The ability to perform as intended and consistently. Site Reliability Engineering (S R E). Applying software engineering to operations to make systems more reliable. Observability. Being able to understand a system's internal state from its outputs (logs, metrics, traces). Exam tip: Event equals something happened (may be fine). Incident equals something broke or got worse.

1.title: Deliver
1.text: Deliver. Purpose: provide the services to consumers as agreed and respond to their requests. Service request. A request from a user for something that is part of normal service delivery, such as access or information. A service request is not an incident: nothing is broken.

1.title: Support
1.text: Support. Purpose: restore normal operation when something goes wrong, help users, and feed what is learned back into the product and service. Disaster. A sudden, unplanned event that causes great damage or loss and stops critical work. Problem. A cause or potential cause of one or more incidents. Error. A flaw or malfunction in a component that can cause incidents. Known error. A problem that has been analyzed but not yet resolved, usually with a workaround. Workaround. A solution that reduces or removes the impact without fixing the cause.

1.title: Support, continued
1.text: Support. The figure shows this: Problem, error and known error compared with incident. Exam tip: Incident equals the interruption. Problem equals the cause under investigation. Error equals the fault. Known error equals the problem is understood, not yet fixed, workaround exists.

1.title: All eight at a glance
1.text: All eight at a glance. Transition. go live safely. Operate. run as agreed. Deliver. provide the service. Support. restore and help.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A team releases every change that passes automated tests directly to live without human approval. Which practice is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Continuous deployment. Automatic release to live is continuous deployment.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A payment service is unavailable for twenty minutes. What is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: An incident. An unplanned interruption of a service is an incident.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which statement is C O R R E C T? (one) A known error is a problem that has been analyzed but not resolved. (two) A service request is the same as an incident. (three) A workaround reduces or removes the impact without fixing the cause. (four) An event always means something has failed. The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: one and three. Known errors and workarounds are defined that way.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Identify the missing word(s). blank is the ability to understand a system's internal state from its outputs. The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Observability. That is observability.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A user asks for access to a shared drive. Which term describes the request? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Service request. It is a normal request, not a failure.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. The cause of repeated outages has been found, no fix exists yet, and the team uses a documented workaround. What is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A known error. The problem is understood but not resolved, and a workaround exists.

1.title: Practice Question 7
1.text: Question seven. Which activity has the purpose of moving a new or changed product safely into live use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Transition. That is the purpose of transition.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Define an incident. Answer: An unplanned interruption or reduction in the quality of a service. Question two. Define an event. Answer: Any change of state that has significance for managing a product or service. Question three. What is the difference between continuous delivery and continuous deployment? Answer: Delivery keeps every change ready to release; deployment releases every passing change automatically.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Define a problem. Answer: A cause or potential cause of one or more incidents. Question five. What is a known error? Answer: A problem that has been analyzed but not resolved, usually with a workaround. Question six. What does S R E stand for? Answer: Site Reliability Engineering.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Transition or operate or deliver or support: go live or run or provide or restore and help. Release: a version made available for use. C D: delivery equals ready; deployment equals automatic. Event or incident: change of state or unplanned interruption. Problem or error or known error: cause or fault or analyzed, unresolved, workaround. Service request: normal request, nothing broken.
